name: Route analysis: bus routes compared (route_compare.json)
plain: One row for each of 97 bus routes of the ATI and of the municipal systems of the San Juan metro area and eastern Puerto Rico, compared on five measures from their weekday timetables: service, route, peak-hour intersections, connections and nearby residents. It describes the scheduled service, not the service observed on the street.
definition: route_compare.json has two tables. routes: one record per operator and route label with a bus trip in the weekday timetable (typical Wednesday) of the ATI or of San Juan, Bayamón, Guaynabo, Caguas, Canóvanas (the metro area: a stop within 250 m of an ATI stop), Fajardo, Humacao, Juncos, San Lorenzo, Patillas or Vieques (the east), with the 30 fields of route_compare.*. operators: the 12 systems, with their name and the end date of their timetable (feed_end). The Tren Urbano is left out (its own track).
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/route_compare.py reads site/data (trips.json, transport.json, transit_routes.geojson, population_blocks.json) and four inputs from the road-features analysis, committed beside it: road_features.geojson (OpenStreetMap junctions and footbridges), road_flow.csv (their estimated design-hour volume from FHWA HPMS 2024: AADT x K factor), transit_exposure.csv and transit_runtime.csv (when each route's trips pass them, and its scheduled run times); make_page.py publishes the result as this file and writes the page.
how_to_read: Compare routes within the same kind of timetable. A route with a full timetable (a time at every stop) is measured on its timed path; a timetable-only route (two timed stops) on the operator's line, so its length, speed and crossings are marked with an asterisk on the page.
caveats: Timetables, not observed service: delays and skipped trips are not seen.

The flow that defines a high-volume intersection is an estimate of the design-hour volume (AADT x K factor: the 30th-busiest hour of the year), not a count and not a typical weekday peak; 48% of the junctions use the observatory's class-median K, which HPMS guidance does not endorse.
Four timetables had expired on 2026-10-19 (Caguas, Fajardo, Juncos, San Lorenzo) and Canóvanas's ends on 2026-10-31.
Cataño and Toa Baja publish no GTFS timetable, so their routes are missing.

name: Morning peak trips, busiest direction
plain: How many trips leave from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. on the route's busiest stop pattern (one direction).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: Morning peak headway
plain: Every how many minutes, on average, the route runs from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. in its busiest direction.
definition: 180 minutes divided by peak_trips_one_direction, rounded to the minute. Blank when no trip leaves in that period.
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: round(180 / peak_trips_one_direction).
how_to_read: Planners often treat 15 minutes or less as service people can use without a timetable.
caveats: An average over three hours: two trips that leave together still count as two.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: Route length
plain: The length of the route's main stop pattern, in kilometers. For a timetable-only route it is the length of the line the operator draws, which can hold both directions.
definition: Meters along the path of the stop pattern with most trips (trips.json paths), in km to one decimal. For a timetable-only route (timepoints_only: Bayamón, Caguas, Juncos and San Lorenzo, and ATI express route 20), the operator's route line in transit_routes.geojson is used instead of the timed path. Its longest part is measured, and it may draw the outbound and return trips as one line (Bayamón BR-1: 32.1 km of line, 16.0 km between its two timed stops).
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: route_compare.py: path[-1][2] / 1000, or the route line's length for a timetable-only route.
caveats: Marked with an asterisk on the page for timetable-only routes: it is the line drawn, not one trip.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: Scheduled speed
plain: The average speed the timetable plans for the route's main stop pattern, from its first to its last timed stop.
definition: Length of the timed path divided by the median scheduled time from first to last stop of the main pattern's trips, in km/h. Blank for a timetable-only route whose timed path is under half its route line (the timed stretch is not the whole trip).
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: route_compare.py: path_km / (median run / 3600); set blank when timepoints_only and path_km < 0.5 x line length.
caveats: Scheduled, not observed.
A timetable with long waits at stops gives a low speed.
Marked with an asterisk on the page for timetable-only routes: the speed of the stretch between their two timed stops.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: High-volume intersections on the path
plain: How many signalized junctions and roundabouts with an estimated 2,000 or more vehicles an hour in the design hour (one of the busiest hours of the year) lie on the route's path.
definition: Signalized junctions and roundabouts (OpenStreetMap, road_features.geojson) within 20 m of the route's paths whose estimated design-hour volume (road_flow.csv: AADT x K factor of the busiest FHWA HPMS road within 30 m; K is the 30th-busiest hour of the year as a percentage of AADT, HPMS Field Manual item 26; for 48% of the junctions the observatory's class-median K) is 2,000 vehicles an hour or more. For a timetable-only route (timepoints_only: Bayamón, Caguas, Juncos and San Lorenzo, and ATI express route 20), the operator's route line in transit_routes.geojson is used instead of the timed path.
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: transit_exposure.csv (busy_junctions_on_path, written by the road-features analysis's transit_exposure.py), or a 20 m buffer of the route line for a timetable-only route.
caveats: The flow is an estimate from annual averages, not a count at the hour.
20 m can catch a junction the route passes over or under.
The flow is that of the busiest road at the junction, not necessarily the one the bus uses.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: High-volume intersections per 10 km
plain: High-volume intersections on the path for every 10 km of route.
definition: busy_junctions x 10 / length_km, to one decimal.
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: route_compare.py.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: Morning peak crossings of high-volume intersections
plain: How many times, added over all its trips, the route's buses pass a high-volume intersection from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m.
definition: Each weekday trip is placed on its path by its stop times (time between two stops spread by distance), which gives the time it passes each high-volume intersection; the passes between 6:00 and 9:00 are counted. For a timetable-only route it is estimated as the trips leaving 6:00-9:00 times busy_junctions (passes_estimated).
geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

method: transit_exposure.csv (busy_passes_6_9), or route_compare.py's estimate.
how_to_read: A measure of expected exposure to congestion, not of delay: the timetables do not say how long a bus waits at a junction.
caveats: Marked with an asterisk on the page when estimated.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

name: Afternoon peak crossings of high-volume intersections

geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.
